mcqs.question: A student can read a book held close to the eye clearly, but objects at a distance appear blurred. Which term best describes this condition?

options.A: Myopia – inability to see distant objects clearly
options.B: Hypermetropia – inability to see near objects clearly
options.C: Astigmatism – distortion of vision at all distances
options.D: Presbyopia – age‑related loss of near vision

mcqs.answer: Myopia – inability to see distant objects clearly
mcqs.explanation: Myopia (short‑sightedness) is characterized by clear near vision and blurred distant vision because the image of distant objects is formed in front of the retina. Options B, C and D describe different defects, not the condition described.

mcqs.question: Riya spends many hours each day reading textbooks at a distance of about 30 cm. Over time she notices that she can no longer see the blackboard clearly. What is the primary anatomical cause of her difficulty?

options.C: Excessive axial length of the eyeball
options.D: Decrease in the power of the crystalline lens

mcqs.answer: Excessive axial length of the eyeball
mcqs.explanation: Myopia is mainly caused by an eyeball that is too long (or a cornea that is too curved), so parallel rays from distant objects converge before reaching the retina. Option C states this cause. Options A and B describe opposite or unrelated changes, and D is not a cause of myopia.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements about correcting myopia with spectacles is correct?

options.A: Concave lenses diverge light and are used to correct myopia
options.B: Convex lenses converge light and are used to correct myopia
options.C: Myopia can be corrected by wearing glasses with positive (convex) power
options.D: Myopia does not require any lens correction

mcqs.answer: Concave lenses diverge light and are used to correct myopia
mcqs.explanation: Myopia is corrected by placing a diverging (concave) lens in front of the eye, which shifts the focal point back onto the retina. Options B and C describe convex lenses, which are used for hypermetropia, not myopia. Option D is false because most myopes need corrective lenses.

mcqs.question: A person can see distant objects clearly but struggles to read a book held at arm’s length. Which refractive error does this describe?
mcqs.explanation: Hypermetropia (far‑sightedness) is characterized by clear distant vision and blurred near vision because the image of near objects is formed behind the retina. Option B matches this description; the other options describe different conditions.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly explains the primary cause of hypermetropia, in contrast to myopia?

options.A: Hypermetropia is caused by a shorter axial length of the eye, causing the image to focus behind the retina
options.B: Hypermetropia is caused by an excessively long axial length, causing the image to focus in front of the retina
options.C: Hypermetropia is caused by a flatter cornea, moving the focal point behind the retina
options.D: Hypermetropia is caused by increased lens thickness, moving the focal point in front of the retina

mcqs.answer: Hypermetropia is caused by a shorter axial length of the eye, causing the image to focus behind the retina
mcqs.explanation: In hypermetropia the eyeball is shorter (or cornea less curved) so parallel rays focus behind the retina; the eye needs converging power to bring the image forward. Option A states this correctly. Options B and D describe myopia, while C is partially true but not the primary cause emphasized in NCERT.

mcqs.question: A hypermetropic eye requires which type of corrective lens to move the focal point onto the retina?
mcqs.explanation: Hypermetropia is corrected by a converging (convex) lens that adds positive power, moving the focal point forward onto the retina. Concave lenses (A) are for myopia. Plano lenses have no power, and bifocals are used for presbyopia, not primary hypermetropia correction.

mcqs.question: Select the correct definition of myopia:

options.A: Myopia – difficulty in seeing distant objects clearly
options.B: Hypermetropia – difficulty in seeing distant objects clearly
options.C: Astigmatism – difficulty in seeing near objects clearly
options.D: Presbyopia – difficulty in seeing at any distance

mcqs.answer: Myopia – difficulty in seeing distant objects clearly
mcqs.explanation: Myopia (short‑sightedness) means distant objects are blurred because the image forms in front of the retina. Option A gives the correct definition; the other options describe different visual defects.

mcqs.question: Which of the following best explains why myopia develops?

options.A: The eye is too short, causing images to focus behind the retina
options.B: The cornea is too flat, causing images to focus behind the retina
options.C: The eye is too long or the cornea too curved, causing images to focus in front of the retina
options.D: The crystalline lens loses flexibility with age

mcqs.answer: The eye is too long or the cornea too curved, causing images to focus in front of the retina
mcqs.explanation: Myopia results from an elongated eyeball or overly curved cornea, so parallel rays converge before reaching the retina. Option C captures this mechanism. Option A describes hypermetropia, B is incorrect curvature direction, and D refers to presbyopia, not myopia.
